the EM algorithm for the RBF learning is a powerful learning technique, the alternative ME model and the ENRBF nets are the preferred architecture for the RBF nets, and that the proposed model selection criterion is able to determine the optimal number of basis functions.

the EM algorithm for the alternative ME and RBF models is able to determine all the parameters in the input and output layers of the ME and RBF architectures simultaneously, and that the proposed adaptive algorithm and the criterion can further improve the performance of the learning and model selection.

(1) the NRBF net and ENRBF net have the same capability of the ME model for modeling complex nonlinear functions, and the NRBF net is a special case of the ENRBF nets, and (2) the alternative ME model can be linked to the NRBF net as well as the ENRBF network.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of new RBF nets and ME models, and the proposed learning technique, CCl, adaptive learning, and the new criterion are all shown to be useful for improving learning performance and/or reducing learning time.
a novel learning technique, a number of new algorithms and a new learning system for mixture of experts and RBF nets.
a number of important issues in learning and modeling of RBF nets, including learning algorithms and criteria, model selection, and the capability for curve fitting and detection.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the alternative ME model is the most powerful and flexible model for mixture of basis functions.

the proposed EM algorithm for NRFB nets and ENRFB nets is a powerful and efficient technique for function approximation and curve detection, and the proposed adaptive algorithm is able to improve considerably the prediction and investment performance of the NRBF nets and the alternative ME.

the proposed learning technique is able to provide a new and effective approach to learning and model selection for RBF nets and the alternative ME models, and the proposed criterion for determining the number of basis function and the number of experts can be a useful tool for model selection.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the alternative ME model is a good alternative to the conventional ME model, and the proposed EM algorithm for NRFB nets and ENRFB nets as well as CCL and adaptive learning are effective and efficient learning techniques for RBF nets.
the proposed learning technique is a promising alternative to the conventional RBF nets and multilayer perceptron nets.

, the proposed learning technique is a promising one for RBF nets and ME model, the proposed criterion for model selection is a new and useful one, and that the proposed adaptive learning technique is an important one for financial prediction and investment.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the alternative ME model is more suitable than the original model for modeling the nonlinear regression problem, and it is also shown to have the same learning capability as the ENRBF nets, which are the alternative model for the original ME model.

the EM algorithm is able to learn NRBF and ENBF nets globally, and the proposed adaptive algorithm can speed up the learning significantly with only a slight loss of performance accuracy, and that the proposed model selection criterion is effective for the number of basis function determination.

the RBF nets, mixture of experts, and Bayesian learning are all closely related to each other and that the EM algorithm for the RBF nets and the alternative ME models can provide a better alternative to the existing RBF nets and ME learning methods.
